Calculus worked for a hundred and fifty years on a vague idea of “continuous quantity” inherited from Eudoxus and Euclid. In 1817 Bolzano published a proof of the intermediate value theorem and realised that he was missing a property of the numbers that nobody had written down. And in 1872, in the same year, Dedekind and Cantor published two different constructions of $\mathbb{R}$: Dedekind with his cuts —defining a real as the cut it produces in the rationals— and Cantor with Cauchy sequences.
